articles.title: Two beluga whales expected to leave Monday headed for Shedd Aquarium
articles.description:
The last of Marineland Canada’s beluga whales were expected to leave the shuttered aquatic park Monday, with two heading for Shedd Aquarium, according to Canadian media reports.

“There will no longer be any beluga whales or any other type of whales in captivity in Canada at the end of today,” Andrew Burns, Marineland’s adviser, told The Canadian Press.

Four more belugas were headed to SeaWorld in San Antonio, according to the news agency.

Monday’s departures means 30 belugas and four dolphins have been shipped out of Marineland for four U.S. aquariums and one in Spain.

The shipment comes on the heels of a Shedd announcement last week that one of the Marineland belugas — Peekachu, a 23-year-old female — had died. Shedd has not released a cause of death, but staff there said last week that Peekachu had not been consistently eating a full diet since her arrival and that there were concerns she was dehydrated.

Peekachu was part of a group of four belugas that arrived Aug. 13, joining four other beluga rescues that arrived from Marineland Canada July 21. In total, Shedd had expected to house 18 belugas, including the eight already living at the aquarium before the Marineland whales arrived and the two expected to leave Canada Monday. That number is now down to 17.

The Marineland belugas had been living at the park, which has for years faced criticism that its animals were living in unsanitary conditions. The park closed to the public in 2024 and Marineland officials, citing extreme financial difficulties, had threatened to euthanize the whales if permanent homes couldn’t be found.

articles.title: Repairing the Grand Canyon's critical water supply line will be tricky
articles.description: The sole pipeline that supplies water for millions of Grand Canyon visitors was badly damaged by weekend flash flooding, setting up a tricky repair scenario and upending a yearslong construction project to upgrade the line. The Transcanyon Waterline traverses terrain so rugged that helicopters are often required to make basic repairs. Park officials say roughly 40% of of the 12.5-mile-long line was damaged or destroyed. It has endured dozens of breaks in recent years and was undergoing a more than $200 million repair and replacement project when the floods hit. The rugged terrain makes any effort to fix breaks time-consuming, precarious and costly, so efforts to address the latest damage will be complicated.

articles.title: Vanuatu Ministry of Health: Watery Diarrhoea Outbreak in Tanna Island, Tafea Province - Situation Update No. 1 - Report Date: 25 August 2026 I Reporting Period: 10-21 August 2026
articles.description: Country: Vanuatu Source: Government of Vanuatu Please refer to the attached file. Overview From 10 August to 25 August 2026, a total of 81 cases of watery diarrhoea were reported through Lenakel Hospital. The weekly number of reported cases exceeded the outbreak alert threshold of 34 cases, resulting in the declaration of a watery diarrhoea outbreak in Tanna Island. Most cases were reported through Lenakel Hospital. Hotspot communities include Lounuloul, Imai, Isla, Lamtavekel, Loueiau, and lmarap. Case definition: Three or more loose or watery stools within a 24-hour period. Key highlights: 81 cases reported between 10 and 25 August 2026. Cases exceeded the outbreak alert threshold, resulting in the declaration of an outbreak. Most cases are among children under 5 years of age. Seven cases have been hospitalised, with one severe case reported and no deaths to date. Stool samples have been collected and are awaiting laboratory results to identify the causative agent. Community awareness, enhanced surveillance, and case management activities are ongoing.
